title: In The Long Run, Nvidia NVSwitch Is The InfiniBand Of Scale Up AI Networks
gist: Nvidia's InfiniBand and Ethernet/NVSwitch interconnect revenues have converged (roughly $25.7B each trailing twelve months), and while Ethernet is set to dominate scale-out AI networking, the author argues NVSwitch will persist as the entrenched standard for scale-up GPU-memory fabrics much as InfiniBand did in HPC, even as UALink and ESUN coalitions of Nvidia's own customers race to unseat it.

insights.claim: Mellanox acquired InfiniBand switch rival Voltaire for $218 million in November 2010, consolidating its position as the dominant InfiniBand switch and NIC supplier.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Illustrates the historical pattern of InfiniBand market consolidation around a single dominant supplier, the same dynamic now repeating with Nvidia as the sole current InfiniBand vendor.
insights.locator: Mellanox bought Voltaire for $218 million in November 2010

insights.claim: Intel acquired QLogic's InfiniBand business for $125 million in January 2012, and that team was later spun back out to become Cornelis Networks in September 2020.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Shows repeated cycles of large vendors entering and exiting the InfiniBand market, useful precedent for judging how durable today's vendor commitments to Ethernet-based AI networking standards will be.
insights.locator: which was acquired by Intel for $125 million in January 2012

insights.claim: Oracle kept using InfiniBand in HPC clusters after acquiring Sun Microsystems for $5.6 billion in April 2009 and buying InfiniBand switch maker Xsigo Systems, but ultimately decided Ethernet would be its scale-up, scale-out, and scale-across networking platform.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A major hyperscale-adjacent vendor already made the InfiniBand-to-Ethernet pivot years ago, a precedent for today's AI hyperscalers doing the same across their clusters.
insights.locator: Oracle continued this for a whole after it bought Sun Microsystems

insights.claim: The author estimates Nvidia generated about $25.74 billion in InfiniBand revenue over the trailing twelve months through July, almost matching the roughly $25.67 billion the author estimates Nvidia made from combined Ethernet and NVSwitch interconnect sales over the same period.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Quantifies that Nvidia's non-InfiniBand (Ethernet/NVSwitch) networking revenue has now caught up to its InfiniBand revenue, an inflection point for modeling Nvidia's networking segment mix.
insights.quote: Nvidia has made $25.74 billion in the trailing twelve fiscal months ending in July. This is almost the same as the $25.67 billion that I think Nvidia sold for Ethernet and NVSwitch interconnects combined.
insights.locator: which is why I think Nvidia has made $25.74 billion

insights.claim: This convergence likely marks peak InfiniBand for large AI clusters, as hyperscalers, cloud builders, and AI model builders increasingly standardize on emerging Ultra Ethernet technology, while Ethernet ASIC vendors including Broadcom, Cisco Systems, and Nvidia itself keep reducing port-hop and end-to-end latency in their fabrics.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Signals a structural long-term shift in AI datacenter interconnect spend away from InfiniBand toward Ethernet-based fabrics, relevant to positioning of Ethernet switch/ASIC vendors versus Nvidia's InfiniBand franchise.
insights.quote: But this is probably peak InfiniBand for large clusters
insights.locator: But this is probably peak InfiniBand for large clusters, with so many hyperscalers

insights.claim: Nvidia currently accounts for roughly 95% of GPU revenue and about 75% of combined GPU/XPU revenue, giving it dominant share of scale-up networking via NVLink/NVSwitch, a share the author expects to erode by only a few percentage points through calendar 2027.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Quantifies Nvidia's near-term (through 2027) scale-up networking dominance as highly durable despite emerging standards competition, a bullish near-term data point tempered by the longer-run erosion thesis elsewhere in the piece.
insights.locator: For now, with Nvidia accounting for maybe 95 percent of the GPU revenues

themes.theme: NVSwitch as the Long-Run Scale-Up Standard

insights.claim: The article's central argument is that NVSwitch is positioned to become as durable and entrenched a standard for scale-up, intra-rack GPU memory networking as InfiniBand has been for high-performance computing interconnects over more than two decades, even as Ethernet comes to dominate scale-out AI cluster networking.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The article's central investment thesis: NVSwitch could retain a durable moat in scale-up AI networking analogous to InfiniBand's persistence, which matters for how investors weight Nvidia's networking (not just GPU) revenue durability.
insights.locator: For the record, I love InfiniBand, and I love NVSwitch

insights.claim: Nvidia's NVLink/NVSwitch fabric currently links up to 72 accelerators into one coherent shared-memory domain, expandable to 576 devices at the cost of added latency hops.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Defines the current technical ceiling of Nvidia's scale-up fabric that rival protocols like UALink are explicitly targeting to beat.
insights.locator: Ethernet is also making its way into the scale up domain of Nvidia's NVSwitch interconnects

themes.theme: Scale-Up Standards War: UALink vs. ESUN

insights.claim: UALink, founded in May 2024 by AMD, Broadcom, Cisco, Google, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Intel, Meta Platforms, and Microsoft, directly challenges NVLink/NVSwitch for scale-up AI networking; AMD is already using Broadcom Tomahawk 6 Ultra Ethernet switches to run the UALink protocol inside its 'Helios' racks.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A broad, well-capitalized coalition of Nvidia's own customers and competitors is already shipping product (AMD's Helios racks) on a rival scale-up standard, a concrete near-term competitive threat to NVSwitch lock-in.
insights.locator: This includes UALink, which fired the first salvo at NVLink and NVSwitch

insights.claim: A separate ESUN protocol, backed by Meta and Microsoft and joined by AMD, Arista Networks, Arm, Cisco, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Marvell, Nvidia itself, OpenAI, and Oracle, splits the Ethernet scale-up stack into two layers, with the SUE-T layer handling load balancing, as another alternative to NVLink/NVSwitch.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia itself is hedging by participating in the rival ESUN effort even while pushing its own proprietary NVLink Fusion, signaling it is not fully certain NVSwitch will win outright long-term.
insights.locator: So is the ESUN protocol espoused by Meta Platforms and Microsoft

insights.claim: Broadcom has walked away from the UALink coalition and, as far as the author knows, is not currently interested in the NVLink/NVSwitch combination either, though that could change if its custom-chip design customers want to standardize on Nvidia-style racks.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Broadcom's hedging stance on scale-up standards is a swing factor; its custom silicon customers' choices could tip momentum toward or away from NVSwitch as a shared rackscale fabric.
insights.locator: Broadcom is part of the ESUN/SUE-T effort

insights.claim: UALink 1.0, launched in April 2025, can scale to 1,024 XPUs or GPUs within a single tier of switching, versus an estimated two tiers of NVSwitch needed to link 576 GPUs, giving UALink a theoretical scale advantage.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A concrete technical benchmark investors can use to judge whether UALink's scale claims translate into deployments that undercut Nvidia's scale-up fabric advantage.
insights.locator: The UALink 1.0 spec, launched in April 2025, can scale to 1,024 XPUs or GPUs

insights.claim: InfiniBand's port-hop latency of about 100 to 120 nanoseconds is one-third to one-half that of Ethernet switches; the UALink spec aims for roughly 100-nanosecond port hops without requiring it, while NVSwitch's port-hop latency is rumored, but never confirmed, to be closer to Ethernet than to InfiniBand.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: If the NVSwitch latency rumor is true, it hands UALink a real technical edge over Nvidia's scale-up fabric if UALink vendors can achieve InfiniBand-like latencies, an unresolved data point worth watching for confirmation.
insights.quote: NVSwitch port hops are rumored to be more like Ethernet than InfiniBand, but no one has ever confirmed this
insights.locator: InfiniBand, at 100 nanoseconds to 120 nanoseconds, has one third to one half the latency

themes.theme: Nvidia-MediaTek Deal and NVLink Fusion Strategy

insights.claim: Nvidia purchased $3.5 billion in convertible bonds issued by Taiwanese SoC maker MediaTek, with CEO Jensen Huang calling MediaTek the biggest and best maker of SoCs in the world on Bloomberg; as part of the deal, MediaTek gains access to the NVLink Fusion stack to put NVLink ports on its own chips.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A direct capital commitment by Nvidia to widen the NVLink/NVSwitch ecosystem to a major merchant SoC vendor, a concrete move to expand its scale-up fabric's addressable silicon base ahead of the UALink/ESUN threat.
insights.quote: the biggest and best maker of SoCs in the world
insights.locator: Today, Nvidia bought $3.5 billion in convertible bonds issued by Taiwanese SoC maker MediaTek

insights.claim: Nvidia does not sell NVSwitch ASICs or switch complexes as a standalone product; customers must buy an Nvidia Grace or Vera CPU or a Blackwell or Rubin GPU plus Nvidia's own racks to get NVSwitch scale-up networking, though the author speculates Nvidia could eventually open NVSwitch networking to any NVLink-port-equipped chip.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Highlights Nvidia's current vertical-bundling strategy as a margin and lock-in lever; an eventual opening of NVSwitch as a merchant product would be a major strategic shift for investors to watch for.
insights.locator: Nvidia is not selling NVSwitch ASICs and complexes separately

insights.claim: NVLink Fusion, which extends NVLink access to third-party chipmakers like MediaTek, is characterized as an explicit effort by Nvidia to undercut and delay the rival UALink and ESUN/SUE-T standards by a generation or two.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Frames NVLink Fusion as a defensive, delaying tactic rather than a permanent moat; investors should expect continued erosion pressure on Nvidia's scale-up networking share over a multi-year horizon even as near-term dominance holds.
insights.quote: The NVLink Fusion is an effort to put a spanner in the UALink and ESUN/SUE-T works, to stall the inevitable for another generation or two.
insights.locator: The NVLink Fusion is an effort to put a spanner in the UALink and ESUN/SUE-T works

insights.claim: The author predicts that even if UALink displaces NVLink/NVSwitch as the de facto scale-up standard, Nvidia would simply become the leading UALink switch and port vendor and still generate on the order of $100 billion from the transition, mirroring how it profits from InfiniBand today despite Ethernet's dominance in scale-out networking.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Reframes the UALink competitive threat as far less existential for Nvidia's revenue than a naive standards-war framing suggests; Nvidia likely wins financially regardless of which scale-up standard ultimately prevails.
insights.quote: Nvidia will just make the best damned UALink switches and ports that it can, and it will have made maybe $100 billion on NVLink/NVSwitch.
insights.locator: And guess what happens if UALink succeeds and becomes the de facto scale up network standard?

insights.claim: The author predicts the UALink and ESUN/SUE-T camps will likely eventually merge into a unified 'UALink 2.0' standard, drawing an analogy to how the CXL memory-coherency standard emerged from consolidation of earlier rival efforts, and to how Google, Microsoft, and Arista Networks forced the IEEE to adopt 25 Gb/sec signaling for 100 Gb Ethernet in 2014 after growing frustrated with the slow-moving standards body.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Suggests the fragmented scale-up standards landscape is likely to consolidate into one dominant open alternative to NVLink/NVSwitch, presenting a more unified long-term competitive threat to Nvidia than either standard alone.
insights.locator: There is a chance – someone might even say a probability – that the UALink and ESUN/SUE-T camps will bury the hatchet
